# Conclusion

Over 9 years, *Sasa* expanded on the study slope with a net change of +19% (gross expansion 48%, gross loss 29%). Establishment probability was most strongly associated with proximity to existing patches, with further variation associated with snowmelt regime and topography. Environmentally suitable area greatly exceeded occupied area, suggesting that dispersal limitation accounts for the gap. A process model calibrated to observed change projected approximately 4,900–5,700 m² of further establishment by 2030 under scenarios conditioned on the observed decade rather than forecasts of snowmelt, concentrated in snowbed communities adjoining current patches and only modestly sensitive to earlier snowmelt. Using *Sasa* as an example, this study shows that ground-based time-lapse imagery fills the gap between plot surveys and satellite observations, allowing metre-scale expansion to be observed and projected at the resolution of the process itself.
